adds.title: LGBT rights in Turkey — Wikipedia
adds.summary: Turkey permits transgender people to change their legal gender since 1988 (with surgery and court approval) but has no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity; same-sex marriage, civil unions and adoption are unavailable, and because marriage eligibility is determined by the gender recorded in the civil registry rather than by trans status, a person who has legally changed registered gender may marry a partner of the opposite registered gender. When the 12th judicial reform package passed in 2026, provisions discriminating against LGBTQ people were removed from the bill, making only symbolic same-sex weddings possible with no legal marital status. Since 2015 authorities have banned Pride events in Istanbul and other cities in most years, with police using tear gas, water cannons and mass detentions against those who attempt to assemble — the framework under which any visible LGBT assembly in Tokat province would be policed.

adds.title: World Report 2025: Türkiye — Human Rights Watch
adds.summary: HRW's World Report 2025 (covering 2024) records that the government and religious-conservative opposition parties regularly use discriminatory speech amounting to hate speech against LGBT communities on the pretext of promoting family values, which has put LGBT people at great risk. Istanbul Pride was banned for the tenth consecutive year and many cities across the country impose similar bans, so provincial authorities and police in Tokat operate within a nationwide pattern in which visible LGBT assembly is routinely banned and policed.

adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Canada — Wikipedia
adds.summary: Canada's national framework (which applies in British Columbia under section 15 of the Charter of Rights and Freedoms) protects LGBTQ people from discrimination based on sexual orientation; sexual orientation has been covered federally since 1996 and gender identity and gender expression are protected under the Criminal Code hate-propaganda and anti-discrimination provisions. A 2021 Criminal Code amendment, in force since 2022, made Canada the first country in North America to statutorily ban conversion therapy nationwide for both minors and adults, and transgender people may change their legal gender in all provinces and territories under varying rules. The record's claim of no hostile provincial legislation and its national baseline score of 0.86 stand on this framework: Charter equality protection, nationwide conversion-therapy criminalisation, and legal gender change availability in every province including BC.
